q: In solid ionic compounds, their ions are held in fixed positions and cannot move, and they cannot conduct _______. (2024)
e: In solid ionic compounds, ions are held tightly in a rigid crystal lattice and cannot move freely to conduct electricity.

q: A bond's polarity is determined by the _______ of two bonded atoms. (2025)
e: The difference in electronegativity between two bonded atoms determines the dipole moment and bond polarity.

q: The BF₃ molecule, which accepts an _______, behaves as a Lewis acid. (2026)
e: A Lewis acid is defined as an electron pair acceptor, which BF₃ achieves due to its electron-deficient central boron atom.

q: The shape of bromine molecule (Br₂) is _______. (2024)
e: Any diatomic molecule consisting of two bonded atoms forms a straight line and thus has a linear geometry.

q: In solid ionic compounds, their ions are held in _______ positions and cannot move, and hence they cannot conduct electricity. (2025)
e: Ions in solid ionic lattices are restricted to fixed positions and cannot migrate to carry electric current.

q: Fullerene, carbon nanotubes, and graphene are only _______ covalent molecules. (2025)
e: These allotropes of carbon consist of large molecular networks described as bulky covalent structures.

q: Simple cubic unit cell is a cubic cell with an atom in each _______ of the cube. (2025)
e: A simple cubic unit cell contains lattice points positioned exclusively at the eight corners of the cube.

q: The crystalline structure of an ionic solid is called a _______. (2024)
e: Ionic compounds arrange in a continuous, three-dimensional geometric repeating network termed a crystal lattice.

q: The Lewis symbol for carbon is _______. (2024)
e: Carbon possesses four valence electrons, represented by four dots arranged around the atomic symbol C.

q: _______ forces exist between the layers of carbon atoms in graphite. (2025)
e: The planar sheets of carbon atoms in graphite are held together by weak van der Waals forces, allowing them to slide.

q: The CO molecule consists of two covalent bonds and one _______ bond. (2025)
e: In carbon monoxide, the triple bond consists of two normal covalent bonds and one coordinate dative bond donated by oxygen.

q: Ionic bonding depends on the difference in _______ between two atoms. (2024)
e: A large electronegativity difference leads to complete electron transfer, resulting in ionic bond formation.

q: Since electron loss always equals electron gain in an electron transfer process, _______ compounds are always neutral. (2025)
e: Because total positive charges of cations balance total negative charges of anions, ionic compounds are overall electrically neutral.

q: The strength of sharing or transferring the valence electrons depends on the _______ of the atoms involved in the chemical bonding. (2025)
e: Electronegativity determines the relative attraction an atom exerts on electrons during chemical bond formation.

q: The shape of CCl₄ according to the VSEPR model is _______. (2025)
e: Carbon tetrachloride has four bonding electron pairs and zero lone pairs around carbon, adopting a tetrahedral geometry.

q: The _______ chloride ions are needed to cancel the 2+ charge of magnesium in magnesium chloride. (2025)
e: Two Cl⁻ ions (1- each) are necessary to neutralize one Mg²⁺ ion in the neutral ionic formula MgCl₂.

q: _______ bond is characterised by the fact that the two shared electrons are both donated by one of the participating atoms. (2024)
e: A coordinate covalent bond occurs when both electrons in the shared pair originate from the same atom.

q: The higher the value of the _______, the greater is the atom's attraction to electrons. (2024)
e: Electronegativity is a quantitative measure of an atom's ability to attract shared electrons towards itself.

q: Many inorganic substances and millions of organic compounds have _______ bonding. (2025)
e: Covalent bonding via electron pair sharing forms the primary backbone of organic molecules and many inorganic compounds.

q: In SF₆ molecule, the sulphur atom is surrounded by _______ electrons. (2025)
e: Sulfur forms six covalent single bonds with six fluorine atoms in SF₆, expanding its octet to 12 valence electrons.

q: Diamond does not conduct electricity because it has no free moving _______. (2025)
e: In diamond, all four valence electrons of each carbon atom are localized in strong localized covalent single bonds.

q: Dipole moment is a measure of the _______ of a covalent bond. (2025)
e: Dipole moment measures the extent of net charge separation across a polar covalent bond.

q: Valence electrons are the electrons in the _______ shell of an atom. (2025)
e: Valence electrons reside in the outermost electron shell of an atom and participate directly in chemical bonding.

q: Silicon (IV) oxide, SiO₂ (silica or quartz) is an example of a _______ covalent molecule. (2024)
e: Silicon dioxide forms a three-dimensional giant covalent network of linked silicon and oxygen atoms.

q: In SiO₂ (quartz), oxygen atoms are formed as bridges between the _______ bonded silicon atoms. (2026)
e: Each silicon atom in SiO₂ connects to four oxygen atoms located at the corners of a tetrahedron.

q: The term _______ is used to express the number of ions surrounding the central ion in the lattice. (2026)
e: Coordination number specifies how many immediate counter-ions surround a central ion within a crystal structure.

q: Although the _______ within molecules are kept together by strong forces, the forces between molecules are weak. (2026)
e: Intramolecular covalent bonds between atoms are strong, while intermolecular forces acting between discrete molecules are weak.

q: There is no _______ atom in CO molecule. (2026)
e: Because carbon monoxide is a diatomic molecule composed of only two atoms, neither atom serves as a central atom.

q: In ionic compounds, the cations and anions are held together by strong _______. (2026)
e: Ionic bonds consist of strong electrostatic attraction forces pulling together oppositely charged cations and anions.
